meta.title: makeyourmindup: AI, unpicked
meta.description: We follow the money, look under the hood and mind the gap. You make your mind up. A free publication on how AI really works, every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

subchannels.label: follow.the.money
subchannels.coverLine: Who gets paid when AI gets bought.
subchannels.oneLiner: How money gets made with AI, and by whom.
subchannels.body: Every AI deal has a bill, and somebody pays it. Every Monday we trace the money from the invoice to the bank account, and show who comes out ahead and who gets stuck with the tab.
subchannels.question: Where does the money move, and who ends up better or worse off?
subchannels.caption: Illustration. The real ones name every source.

when AI gets

subchannels.label: under.the.hood
subchannels.coverLine: Real, or theatre? We take it apart.
subchannels.oneLiner: How it gets built, and why it works.
subchannels.body: Every Wednesday we open up something that shipped and actually works. Every part gets a stamp, real or theatre, so you can see what does the work and what is there for the launch video.
subchannels.question: What actually goes together in a shipped thing, and why did this one work?
subchannels.caption: Illustration. The real ones show the evidence for every stamp.
headline: Real, or
theatre?
We take it apart.

subchannels.label: mind.the.gap
subchannels.oneLiner: The patterns, and where they lead.
subchannels.body: Most weeks, a pile of AI stories look like they have nothing to do with each other. Every Friday we lay the threads side by side, show where they cross, and put a date on what we think happens next.
subchannels.question: What is the pattern, and what does it mean is coming?
subchannels.caption: Illustration. The real ones come with dates and sources.
headline: What's coming,
before it's
obvious.

scoreboard.title: Every piece makes a call. We keep score.
scoreboard.body: Each piece ends with a prediction, a date and how sure we are. When the date arrives, we mark it held, broke or unclear. Misses go up as big as hits.

staff.title: Who makes this.

rows.v: Busy people who want AI explained without the sales pitch
A blind panel of AI judges, then Krish, who gets the final say

link.text: A blind panel of AI judges

staff.bio: Krish writes every piece, reads the audio edition and fronts the Shorts. He has spent sixteen years building commercial businesses across media, tech and telecoms, and now spends most days building with AI.
staff.photoAlt: Krish Raja, editor of makeyourmindup, pushing his glasses up for a closer look

panel.line: Ten judges read every draft blind: no byline, no author, no idea what Krish liked last time. Any of them can stop a piece. None of them can approve one.
panel.hint: Tap a face to meet one.

cards.name: The Preacher-Catcher
cards.says: That last line wants to be a poster. Net.
cards.asks: Does any sentence tell you what to conclude, believe or become?
cards.offLimits: Everything else. Reads for one thing. Has never been moved by a closing line, and is proud of it.
cards.alt: A smug judge in a pith helmet with a butterfly net, a tiny pulpit caught in it

cards.name: The Fact Checker
cards.asks: Who produced this number, when, counting what?
cards.offLimits: Whether the argument is any good. Would check the sums on a birthday card.
cards.alt: A frowning judge with a jeweller's loupe in one eye, holding a ledger

cards.name: The Cold Reader
cards.says: I've had fifteen seconds and half a coffee. What is this?
cards.asks: Fifteen seconds in, can you say what this is about and why it matters to you?
cards.offLimits: Craft. Has never noticed a semicolon. Not a psychic, and has asked us to stop saying so.
cards.alt: A barely awake judge in a dressing gown, with bed hair and a steaming mug

cards.name: The Sceptic
cards.says: Fine. Now argue it with someone who knows.
cards.asks: What would a well-informed person who disagrees say, and does this survive it?
cards.offLimits: Tone and style. Could not be charmed by a brass band.
cards.alt: A judge with arms folded and one eyebrow raised very high

cards.name: The Line Editor
cards.says: Is that an em dash? In this house?
cards.asks: Would a good editor let this line through?
cards.offLimits: Argument, evidence and pictures. Would correct the grammar on a ransom note.
cards.alt: A judge peering over half-moon glasses on a chain, holding an enormous pencil

cards.name: The Art Director
cards.asks: Does the picture carry the argument, or decorate it?
cards.offLimits: Copy. May sigh at a headline. May not touch it. Sighs a lot.
cards.alt: A bald judge in a black polo neck and round black glasses, holding up a thumb

cards.name: The Distribution Judge
cards.says: Sound's off. Thumbnail's the size of a stamp. Still with me?
cards.asks: Does this survive a thumbnail, a muted autoplay and a collapsed first line?
cards.offLimits: Long-form structure. Has not finished a paragraph this decade.*
cards.footnote: *Unverified. The Fact Checker has been told.
cards.alt: A judge staring down at a glowing phone, earbuds dangling unplugged

cards.name: The Continuity Judge
cards.says: We said this three pieces ago. Differently.
cards.asks: Have we said this, contradicted this, or used this angle before?
cards.offLimits: The piece in isolation. Remembers everything we have published and holds it against us.
cards.alt: A judge with a pencil through a bun and a card-index drawer for a chest

cards.name: The Agency Judge
cards.asks: Does a reader finish more able to judge for themselves, or just better informed?
cards.offLimits: Stating the mission. Has the banner ready. The Preacher-Catcher will not let them unroll it.
cards.alt: A judge mid-sentence, holding a rolled-up banner tied shut on a pole

cards.name: The Commissioner
cards.asks: Against everything else we could have run this week, was this the right use of the day?
cards.offLimits: Craft, evidence and pictures. No veto, because opportunity cost is Krish's call. Finds this maddening.
cards.alt: An unimpressed judge with a moustache, a green eyeshade and a waistcoat with a watch chain

cards.name: The Chair
cards.says: The interesting bit is where they split.
cards.asks: Where did the panel disagree, and which vetoes are still standing?
cards.offLimits: Scoring, vetoing and softening a finding. Adds up, names, writes one paragraph. Very comfortable.
cards.alt: A wingback armchair with a calm face on its backrest
cards.footnote: The bar: every judge 7.5 or more, an average of 8.4 or more, and no veto standing.

footer.line: Made in public. Corrections welcome in the Substack comments.
